in each of the old administrative divisions of the Nilgiris there was one place, called De:na:du, De:na:dukombe, or De:na:yi where Kurumbas camped during large festivals and shouted ‘de: de’; hence four localities, shown on maps as Denad, Tenad, Thenad, Taynaad, Denaad, Daynaad, Thenhadu, Tainavd, Dernaad or Thaynaud, are: 1. Kunda De:na:du, a Gauda hamlet 14.5 km. SSW of Ootacamund, belonging to Ba:kola commune (in existence prior to 1812); 2. De:na:du, 10 km. ENE of Kotagiri, head village of De:na:du commune , it consists of three nearby parts, and is the only example of a Badaga fortified village, as its houses and rectangular workspace are enclosed with a high wall: 2a. De:na:du Ki:yafṭi, a Toreya and Wodeya hamlet (ca 20 Wodeya housesin 1970; originally settled from Me:kuna:du and Kunde hamlets; 2b. De:na:du Naduhafti (ca 20 Wodeya, 35 Toreya houses in 1970), 2c. De:na:du Me:latti, or Bendatti ; 3. Daynaad, a hill which overlooks the head of the Si:gu:r ghat pass, ca 2280 m in elevation, 5 km.
